turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Sophia Brown. Date of birth, 3/17/1946. This is a new patient visit. She's here to establish care for a history of dcis. We'll go over the history with the patient. Hello, ms. Brown.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hi. Yes, that's me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Wonderful. I'm doctor stewart. It's lovely to meet you.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: You as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So, you've come to see me today because you had a right breast lumpectomy last year. Is that right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes. On january 20th, 2020.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And how have you been since then? Any problems or concerns?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I'm feeling good. I do my self breast exams religiously now and haven't felt anything since.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Perfect. I want to back up and go over your history so I can make sure everything in your chart is correct and I don't miss anything. So, I'll tell you what we have in your chart from your other providers and you tell me if anything is wrong or missing. Sound good?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sounds good.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Great. So, I have that you were found to have a calcification in your right breast during a mammogram in october 2019. Was that just a normal screening mammogram, or was it done because you felt a lump?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It was just a normal one you're supposed to get every so often.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see. And then it looks like you had an ultrasound of your right breast on november 3rd, 2019, which revealed a mass at the two o'clock position, 11 centimeters from the nipple in the retroareolar region. The report states the mass was point four by two by three centimeters.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, that sounds right. Hard to remember now, though.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yep, definitely. Based on those results, they decided to do an ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy on december 5th, 2019. Pathology results during that biopsy came back as grade two, er positive, pr positive, dcis, or ductal carcinoma in situ.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes. Unfortunately.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I know. Scary stuff. But you had a lumpectomy on january 20th, 2020, which removed the eight millimeter tumor and margins were negative. The pathology confirmed dcis. Looks like they also removed 5 lymph nodes, which, thankfully, were negative for malignancy. That's great!

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I was definitely very relieved.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And your last mammogram was in january 2021? And that was normal.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. So, I feel like I have a good grasp of what's been going on with you now. And you're here today to establish care with me so I can continue to follow you and make sure you're doing well, right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes. Fingers crossed.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Definitely. We'll keep a close eye on you and take good care of you.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay, sounds good.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I have a few more questions for you. When was your last colonoscopy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I had one in 2018 and, if I remember correctly, I had one polyp and that was removed and it wasn't cancerous.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, yes, I see that report now. One polyp in the sigmoid colon which had a benign tubular adenoma. Okay. And when was your last menstrual period?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Gosh. It was probably around 30 years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Do you have children?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do. I have five.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Ah, big family then. That's nice.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes. And they're all having kids of their own now, so it's getting even bigger.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I bet. Sounds like fun.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It is.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Did you have any other pregnancies that were miscarriages or terminations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Really, I did not.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. So for the record, that's g5 p5. And now that you're post-menopausal, are you currently or have you ever been on hormone replacement therapy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: My primary care doctor gave me the option years ago but I decided against it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And on your review systems form, you indicated that you've not had any recent weight loss or gain, headaches, bone pain, urinary symptoms, or blood in the stools. But you did indicate that you have some back pain, joint pain, and high cholesterol. Tell me some more about those.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. So I've seen doctors for all of those. They've said, excuse me, the back and knee pain are age-related. And the cholesterol is a fairly new diagnosis, but I am working on exercise and cutting back on fatty foods to see if I can get it lower without any medication.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And your primary care doctor is following you for that, right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That's correct.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. For medications, I have that you take coq10, vitamin d, vitamin c, fish oil, and elderberry fruit. Is that all right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, and that's all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. So for your medical history, it's high cholesterol and stage 0 er/pr positive invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast. Any surgeries other than the lumpectomy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I did have my tubes tied after my last baby, but that's all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And how about family history?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: My mom had non-hodgkin's lymphoma and my dad had prostate cancer and heart disease, but I think that's it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: All right. Any family history of breast cancer?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: None.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Did any of your children have medical issues or siblings with medical problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do not have any siblings and, thankfully, my children are all healthy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Wonderful. Do you have any history of smoking, illicit drug use, heavy alcohol consumption?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No drugs. I do drink socially, but never more than that. And I used to smoke, but really, everybody did back then and I probably quit about 30 years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Excellent. I have that you're allergic to penicillin. Any other allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope, just penicillin.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. I think that covers it. Hop up here and let me take a look at you. Okay, so let's use the normal new patient exam template. Only change to make is the breast exam. There are no palpable masses, however, there is skin thickening at the medial inferior aspect of the right breast which may be radiation skin changes. In the result section, note that her ecog performance status today is zero. Do you have... Did you have radiation after the lumpectomy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I did. We also talked about endocrine therapy, but I decided against that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. So your exam looks good, no masses, just some skin changes from that radiation. Now, let's go over the plan for you.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay, sounds good.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: As you know, you've had dcis which we'll list in my note as stage zero, er/pr positive, invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast. Your status post-lumpectomy with removal of five lymph nodes that were benign. You also had, um, radiation therapy but declined endocrine therapy. Today's clinical examination shows no evidence of recurrence with the dcis or other malignancy and your mammogram in january, 2021 was also negative for recurrence and malignancy. So, based on all of that, we can just continue to observe you.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. That sounds great. And when do I come back in to see you?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: In a year, but you should have another mammogram in april of 2022 before you come back to see me.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay, I can do that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Wonderful. I'm glad to see you doing so well. Do you have any questions or concerns I can address for you today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, great. My nurse will be in shortly to discharge you. Take care!

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: You as well.
